name: 词性标注分布
description: Analyzes part-of-speech tag distribution patterns to detect AI-generated text, which often shows unnatural grammatical structure distributions.
useCase: Detecting AI text through abnormal grammatical category distributions compared to natural human writing
mechanism: Performs part-of-speech tagging on input text and computes the frequency distribution of each POS category (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc.). AI-generated text tends to over-rely on certain syntactic constructions, producing flatter distributions or unusual ratios between categories (e.g., higher adjective-to-noun ratio). The method compares observed distributions against reference human corpora using chi-squared goodness-of-fit tests.
source: Fröhling & Zubiaga (2021) - Feature-based Detection of Automated Language Models: Tackling GPT-2, GPT-3, and Grover, PeerJ Computer Science
algorithm: POS Tagging + Chi-Squared Goodness-of-Fit + KL Divergence
parameters: POS Tagset: Universal Dependencies, Window: full document, Comparison: reference corpus baselines, Granularity: fine-grained 36-tag
strengths:
• Language-structure based rather than content-based
• Works across different AI model architectures
• Computationally efficient
• Interpretable results for linguists
limitations:
• Requires sufficient text length for reliable statistics
• May vary across text genres and domains
• Advanced AI models increasingly mimic human POS distributions
• Less effective on short texts (<100 words)

references.title: Fröhling, L. & Zubiaga, A. (2021). Feature-based Detection of Automated Language Models: Tackling GPT-2, GPT-3, and Grover. PeerJ Computer Science.
Bakhtin, A. et al. (2019). Real or Fake? Learning to Discriminate Machine from Human Generated Text. arXiv.
